references.text: In the preceding verse, Jesus entrusts a kingdom to the disciples, just as the Father has entrusted it to him. Luke 22:30 elaborates on what this kingdom entails: eating and drinking at his table and sitting on thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel. See [ref:Luk 22:29|Luke 22:29].

Jesus' promise that the disciples will sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel is also found in Matthew. [ref:Matt 19:28|Matthew 19:28] contains an almost identical statement in connection with Peter's question about what the disciples will receive for having left everything.

The promise to share Jesus' throne and dominion with him is reflected in [ref:Rev 3:21|Revelation 3:21], where the one who overcomes will sit with Christ on his throne, just as he himself overcame and sat down with his Father on his throne.
In [ref:Rev 20:4|Revelation 20:4], John sees thrones, and those who sat on them were given authority to judge – a fulfillment of the promise that believers will judge together with Christ.

Paul reminds the Corinthians that the saints will judge the world and angels. [ref:1 Cor 6:2-3|1 Corinthians 6:2-3] confirms the principle that God's people will share in judgment, in line with Jesus' promise in Luke 22:30.
[ref:Dan 7:22|Daniel 7:22] speaks of judgment being given to the saints of the Most High, which forms an Old Testament background for the promise that the disciples will judge the tribes of Israel.

[ref:Dan 7:27|Daniel 7:27] prophesies that the kingdom and dominion will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High – a prophecy that Jesus fulfills by handing over the kingdom and judicial authority to his apostles.

[ref:Isa 25:6|Isaiah 25:6] describes the eschatological meal the Lord will prepare for all peoples on Mount Zion – an image of the messianic feast that Jesus refers to when he speaks of eating and drinking at his table in the kingdom.

[ref:Luk 13:29|Luke 13:29] describes how people will come from east and west, north and south, and sit down at the table in the kingdom of God – a parallel image of the eschatological feast at God's table.
[ref:Luk 14:15|Luke 14:15] mentions the blessing, "Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God", which connects to the same theme of the messianic meal in the kingdom of God.

In [ref:Exod 24:9-11|Exodus 24:9-11], the elders of Israel ate and drank in God's presence on the mountain – a foreshadowing of eating and drinking at God's table in his kingdom, as Jesus promises the disciples.
